thread:
jen: Heads up — staging push for release/2.14 to eu-west-1 failed an integrity/signature check from the publish pipeline, blocking the release window.
deploy-bot: publish: failed provenance verification for image redwood/release-2.14:sha256:8f3a...cb1f in eu-west-1
deploy-bot: error=attestation_missing_or_timestamp_skew details="cosign timestamp missing or outside allowed skew"
sam: Ok, is this a cosign timestamp skew or missing attestation? Any raw logs?
maria: Looks like timestamp skew — seeing `timestamp-server` not present in the attestation metadata. Could be CI VM clock drift or the timestamp server flaked during signing.
I can try a manual resign with a known-good timestamp server.
rachel: If we re-sign, can we just retag to the same digest and promote? Or do we need a full re-publish (new manifest/digest)?
sam: If we re-sign using cosign only the signature layer changes but the manifest/digest may differ depending on how the pipeline attaches attestation. To be safe with immutability we usually republish the same image digest with a new attestation object attached — but our publish bot blocks that unless we do a manual approve.
ops: Recommendation — hold the release (disable auto-promote), create a short maintenance window, do a manual republish+attest using the corporate timestamp server, then let release-bot pick it up.
Command I would run (manual steps):
```
# pull manifest, reattach signed attestation using corporate TS
docker pull eu-west-1.repo.redwood/release-2.14@sha256:8f3a...cb1f
cosign sign --key /secrets/cosign-key --timestamp-server https://timestamp.corp.redwood.internal eu-west-1.repo.redwood/release-2.14@sha256:8f3a...cb1f
aws ecr put-image --repository-name release --image-manifest file://manifest.json --region eu-west-1
```
maria: that looks fine. use `--timestamp-server https://timestamp.corp.redwood.internal` (our internal PKI) instead of the public timestamp endpoint. I'll prepare the attestation payload and a short runbook.
deploy-bot: publishbot: promotion blocked by policy: "attestation:timestamp:valid" failed for image redwood/release-2.14@sha256:8f3a...cb1f — manual override required (approver=release-admin).
jen: Decision: pause the release window for 30m, ops/maria/sam to handle republish. rachel — please update release notes/announce delay and add a note about republish/resign (so customers know why artifact ids are unchanged but timestamps updated). :loud_sound:
rachel: on it. I'll add an entry to the release notes and ping #general when we have an ETA. I'll also flag QA to re-run the smoke tests after republish.
sam: I'll queue the manual republish in ~25m and share the terminal session. tagging plan: keep same semver, do not increment; we'll record the republish in changelog as "artifact re-signed due to timestamp verification".
ops: I'll disable auto-promote for the pipeline (re-enable after we confirm smoke tests). Leaving a temporary hold tag on the release: `release/2.14-hold-177999`.
release-bot: releasebot: auto-promote disabled for release/2.14 by ops (reason="attestation re-sign in progress").
jen: thanks everyone. Ping here when republish completes and before we unhold. :thumbsup:
sam: will do.
